The push was too strong and threw some samples outside the normal action range or into other bad groups.

No edit was accepted for cluster 2. The gate rejected all three submissions, and the session has now used all 20 calls and 3 submissions.

The bad behaviour is one mode on a ring of action modes. That ring rotates as the condition c changes, so the bad mode shows up at about 12% of actions at every c, not only in the card's range of 0.116 to 0.235. Each candidate added a velocity term that rotates the action around the ring into the next mode. A probe on `blocks.2.act` from the `contrast` command decided when it fired.

| Version | Push steps | Target fall (95% CI) | Failed test |
|---|---|---|---|
| v17 | 8–12 | 0.112 [0.107, 0.117] | 5_between |
| v18 | 0–7 | 0.096 [0.091, 0.101] | 3_drift |
| v19 | 4–9, stricter detector threshold | 0.090 [0.085, 0.095] | 3_drift |

- **v17:** pushing late left some actions between modes. My own off-distribution measures in the sandbox showed only about +0.005, so I could not reproduce how the gate scores this test.
- **v18:** pushing early let the flow carry rescued actions onto the next mode, so 5_between passed. But the detector also fires on about 3% of other decodes. Pushed early, those decodes moved too far, and the kept behaviour changed more than test 3 allows.
- **v19:** the middle window with a stricter threshold still failed drift. I could not run quick_check on it because I was out of calls.

A next session could keep the early window and use a more selective detector, such as a per-step probe at k 4–8, to cut the false fires.
